# Verify in production

A change is finished when someone has watched it work. Most changes you can watch **now**, and
that is the rule — this skill is only for the rest: a change whose proof lives somewhere the
repo cannot see yet. You are filing the proof, not doing the work — and the proof itself runs
unattended: an automatic check, end to end, with a person entering
only where no automatic check can exist.

## When it fires: after the merge, never before

**The PR must have merged.** This skill runs as a step of the merge, unasked — `merge-to-main`
calls it once the squash has landed — and at no other moment. Not when the code is written, not
when the PR opens, not while review is in flight.

The reason is that a PR can be **rejected**, and a branch that is still open can be rewritten
under you. Both leave a verification whose premise never reached `main`:

- A **rewritten branch** makes the brief describe a change that no longer exists. #1121 was filed
  against a scope its PR then dropped; the verification was moot before the merge it waited on.
- A **rejected PR** is worse, because the queue cannot tell it from a merge. A blocked item
  releases on its blocker being *closed*, and nothing reads `merged` — so the item goes ready,
  reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by
  `Retry-every:` without comment, and repeats indefinitely. No janitor rule reclaims it: the
  stale-ready sweep cannot see an item sleeping on a future `Not-before`, and the
  stuck-dependency sweep exempts an item whose blockers have closed.

So there is no such thing as filing this early and letting the queue sort it out. Wait for the
merge, then read **what actually landed** — the merged diff, not the branch you remember writing.

## Phase 2 groundwork: two findings from real runs

### 1. The toolchain installs, and the suite can run locally

Flutter **3.47.1** / Dart **3.13.1** (stable, released 2026-08-19) downloads and runs in the agent sandbox. `flutter test` executes, and `matchesGoldenFile` renders and compares **headless on Linux** with no display server — so D9's premise holds against a real run, not an assumption.

This inverts the standing repo rule that Swift/iPad work can only be verified by CI. It is also the version to pin (R6): goldens rendered by one Flutter version are not portable to another.

### 2. Goldens are blind to text until real fonts are loaded — proven, not assumed

`flutter_test` defaults to a glyph-less stub font that draws every character as an identical box. Measured on a minimal widget:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `THE STAND` → `THE STANE` (same length) | **passes** — pixel-identical, undetected |
| `THE STAND` → `THE STANDS AND MORE` (different length) | fails, 17976px / 0.42% diff |

So a golden catches *layout* changes but silently accepts **wrong copy of the same length**. This spec pins exact strings at many leaves — `2.3` `THE STAND · FRI LATE`, `2.4` `8:27 / 20:00`, `2.5` `−11:33`, `2.7` `+1:00`, `4.3` `told`/`live`/`queued`, `4.4` `SET LIST · 4 / 9`, `4.5` `LIVE · 1:24` and `~2:30`, `3.5` `Tap a card to start` — and every one of them would be provable-by-golden in name only.

The executable-requirements pack already warns about exactly this ("test environments default to a glyph-less stub that renders text as boxes"). It is now measured here rather than inherited, and it becomes a hard requirement of PR 2: the harness loads real fonts, and carries a committed test that a same-length copy change reds a golden. Without that test the whole gallery is decorative.

The failure path is good news otherwise: a real mismatch writes `*_isolatedDiff.png`, `*_maskedDiff.png`, `*_masterImage.png` and `*_testImage.png` into `test/failures/`, which is the surface-actual-vs-expected material the re-baselining procedure needs.

import struct
def has(path, cps):
    d=open(path,'rb').read()
    n=struct.unpack('>H',d[4:6])[0]
    off=None
    for i in range(n):
        r=12+16*i
        if d[r:r+4]==b'cmap': off=struct.unpack('>I',d[r+8:r+12])[0]
    if off is None: return None
    nt=struct.unpack('>H',d[off+2:off+4])[0]
    best=None
    for i in range(nt):
        r=off+4+8*i
        pid,eid=struct.unpack('>HH',d[r:r+4])
        so=struct.unpack('>I',d[r+4:r+8])[0]
        if (pid,eid) in ((3,1),(3,10),(0,3),(0,4)): best=off+so
    if best is None: return None
    fmt=struct.unpack('>H',d[best:best+2])[0]
    got=set()
    if fmt==4:
        segX2=struct.unpack('>H',d[best+6:best+8])[0]; seg=segX2//2
        ends=[struct.unpack('>H',d[best+14+2*i:best+16+2*i])[0] for i in range(seg)]
        sb=best+16+segX2
        starts=[struct.unpack('>H',d[sb+2*i:sb+2+2*i])[0] for i in range(seg)]
        for cp in cps:
            for i in range(seg):
                if starts[i]<=cp<=ends[i]: got.add(cp); break
    elif fmt==12:
        ng=struct.unpack('>I',d[best+12:best+16])[0]
        for g in range(ng):
            r=best+16+12*g
            s,e,_=struct.unpack('>III',d[r:r+12])
            for cp in cps:
                if s<=cp<=e: got.add(cp)
    return got

input.body:
First slice of the conversion stack (#40 Phase 2). The Flutter workspace lands **beside** the Swift tree — nothing is deleted, both are live until Phase 3's destructive tail, so `main` stays green throughout.

Closes #45

## The finding this PR is built around

A Flutter test renders text in a glyph-less stub font by default: every character is the same filled box. Measured here before fixing it:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| `THE STAND` → `THE STANE` (same length) | **passes** — byte-identical, undetected |
| `THE STAND` → `THE STANDS AND MORE` (length differs) | fails, 17976px / 0.42% diff |

So a golden catches layout and **silently accepts wrong copy of the same length**. This spec pins exact strings at more than a dozen leaves — `2.3` `THE STAND · FRI LATE`, `2.4` `8:27 / 20:00`, `2.5` `−11:33`, `4.3` `told`/`live`/`queued`, `4.4` `SET LIST · 4 / 9`, `4.5` `LIVE · 1:24` — and every one of them would have been checked in name only.

`loadProductFonts()` reads the families from the bundle's own `FontManifest`, so the harness renders with whatever the product ships; the two cannot drift apart by editing one of them. DejaVu was chosen after checking its `cmap` actually covers the punctuation the copy leans on — the middle dot, a true minus sign (U+2212, not a hyphen), the tilde.

The committed test is the assurance, not a demo: it renders two strings differing by one character and nothing else, and requires the pixels to differ.

## Verification

Everything below was run locally — which is itself new. Flutter 3.47.1 / Dart 3.13.1 installs in the agent sandbox and `matchesGoldenFile` renders and compares headless on Linux with no display server, so **D9's premise holds against a real run**. The standing repo rule that this work can only be verified by CI applied to Swift, and does not carry over.

- `dart test` in `setlist_core` → 2 passed. Watched the tie-break test fail by inverting the comparator.
- `flutter test` in `setlist_ui` → 1 passed. Watched it fail with the fonts unloaded, printing the message it exists to print.
- `node dev/requirements/gate/coverage-gate.mjs` → 57 leaves, 43 claimed, 14 tracked gaps.
